text:
maya: eval-bot flagged a weird regression in nightly for thrush-2 int4 — long prompts start stuttering/repeating after ~120 tokens. repro on local too. failing prompt set: long-dialogue-50. example below.

eval-bot: nightly-eval · model=thrush-2-int4 · suite=long-dialogue-50 · metric=token-repeat-rate · delta=+18% :warning:

maya: example output (expected vs actual):
```
# prompt: user asks about travel itinerary
EXPECTED:
Assistant: Here’s a 5-day itinerary...

ACTUAL:
Assistant: Here’s a 5-day itinerary... day 3 includes a museum visit. day 3 includes a museum visit. day 3 includes a museum visit. day 3 includes a museum visit. ...
```

noah: did we change any kernel selection or batching defaults last deploy? :eyes:

oliver: we rolled the new int4 kernel (opt-kernel v2) to canary yesterday via PR #1328. it was green on perf tests but maybe missed an edge case.

liam: I repro'd locally with the nightly docker image and the repro script. suspect is kv-cache alignment when sequence length jumps after chunking. can you paste the exact command you ran?

maya: running:
```
./ci/run_infer.sh --model thrush-2-int4 --prompt-file tests/long-dialogue-50.txt --batch 1 --max-tokens 512 --reuse-kv true --quant int4
```
attached repro script: `scripts/repro_stutter.sh` (simple loop over prompts)

liam: when I run with `--disable-continuous-batching` the stutter disappears. with batching on, repeat happens.

sophia: that points at batching + kv merge path. quantized kernels have a different memcpy path for KV slices. if offsets are off by a token we can produce repeated context.

liam: logs show this warning right before repetition starts:
```
[warn] kv_cache_offset mismatch: expected=2048 got=2036, copying 128 bytes
[debug] kv_merge(): src_ptr=0x7fabc.. dst_ptr=0x7fdef.. length=512
```

maya: repro artifact: `repro/2026-03-19/thrush2-int4-stutter.log`

oliver: tagging runtime @liam and infra @noah — canary rollback planned?
deploy-bot: deploy · action=rollback · target=canary · component=opt-kernel v2 -> v1.8.2 · status=scheduled

liam: quick patch idea: add an assert that `kv_offset % (head_dim/8) == 0` in quant path and fail fast. also add a unit test that interleaves short+long sequences to catch misaligned copies.

sophia: agree. i'll open a bug: REDWOOD-ML-4123. assign to eng-runtime. will add test and attempt a minimal repro that isolates memcpy vs index arithmetic.

maya: thanks. i'll run a wider sweep of our nightly suites against canary rollback once it's live and report back.

liam: one more datapoint — staging saw similar but less severe when we enabled `kv-prefix-cache` last month. maybe interaction between prefix cache and quant offsets.

noah: pulling up infra logs, I can throttle canary and hold rollback if needed. ETA for rollback 10m.

oliver: ping me when rollback completes and when the unit test lands. if it's low-risk we'll patch the kernel before next rollout.

maya: appreciate the fast triage. adding link to ticket with sample prompts and logs: https://redwood.internal/issue/REDWOOD-ML-4123 :thumbsup:

sophia: will follow up with a short postmortem draft once we have root cause. for now moving flagged nightly jobs to block on canary kernel version.

liam: leaving a small debug flag in runtime (`--kv-check`) to run overnight across the long-dialogue-50 suite; should catch first fail indices. will share logs tomorrow.

maya: great — thanks everyone. :rocket:
